newsitem.title: USA: US economy at or close to full capacity - Dallas Fed.
newsitem.headline: US economy at or close to full capacity - Dallas Fed.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas President Robert McTeer said on Friday that the U.S. economy is operating at or very close to full capacity.
"We are an economy that is operating at or at least very close to full capacity," McTeer told an audience at the Midwestern State University here.
McTeer said the state of the nation's economy is "excellent," adding that inflation is moderate even though labor markets remain tight.
"Labor markets for the last year and a half to two years have been very tight," McTeer said.

"There's been upward pressures on wages. There have been scattered reports of shortages and that's caused people to be concerned about renewed inflation. On the other hand, pipeline inflation has been very moderate," he added.
The Dallas Fed President also said he expected a recent increase in the U.S. short-term interest rates by the central bank would help the economic pot from boiling over.
"Hopefullly, the most recent (Fed) action will help keep the economy from overheating," McTeer said.
The Fed raised its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 percent at the March 25 meeting of its policy-setting body, the Federal Open Market Committee.
